investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 120–146 seconds across all three checks, the agent creation workflow never progressed past pod scheduling, and no VM ID or remote state was ever produced. This is a resource-capacity or node-affinity configuration failure in the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval infrastructure defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs=126899 is well under the outage threshold, so the failure is driven by the Unschedulable condition, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector rules (e.g., a required label such as a kata/peerpods node label is absent or was removed from those nodes), permanently reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource (2 of 6) may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling periods.

QUATERNARY — Pod resource request misconfiguration: the remote agent pod may be requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than necessary, consuming slots faster than expected and accelerating exhaustion.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity > 0 on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., resource quota, admission webhook rejection) should be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient capacity exhaustion that self-resolved, not a persistent misconfiguration.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label and resource but were excluded by a different constraint (e.g., taints, quota), the node affinity hypothesis would need revision.

If the eval runner logs show the pod was never submitted to the Kubernetes API (e.g., an API authentication or agent-creation API error occurred before pod submission), the root cause would shift to the API layer rather than the scheduler.

If sibling checks for non-remote agent features (e.g., local-agent-create) also failed at the same timestamp, a broader infrastructure or authentication issue would be more likely than a kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific capacity problem.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes and alerts when free slots fall below a minimum threshold (e.g., < 2 free slots), providing early warning before pod scheduling failures occur.
Add a node-affinity health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote agent pod and warns if it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure earlier than the current 120s stuck-pod detection.

Consider adding a sibling-correlation eval rule: if all checks within the remote-agents feature fail with the same Unschedulable message pattern, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency (cluster capacity) alert rather than treating each check independently.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod scheduled for a remote agent VM was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence payloads (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced because agent creation never completed, so the state-polling step that depends on a live agent was never reached.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three checks, confirming the failure originates at pod scheduling, not at the application layer. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and the contract-required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, and state were never written (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: four of six nodes are categorically excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto the two kata-capable nodes. If those rules are overly restrictive or stale, capacity appears lower than the physical cluster size.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion can occur even when steady-state capacity is sufficient.

This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 120–146 seconds across all three checks, the agent creation workflow never progressed past pod scheduling, and no VM ID or remote state was ever produced. This is a resource-capacity or node-affinity configuration failure in the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval infrastructure defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 120s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message for 144s, 0/6 nodes available, same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion and affinity mismatch pattern.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message for 146s, confirming the condition persisted across the full eval window (~7 minutes from 04:39 to 04:46 UTC).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never being scheduled and the agent creation call never returning.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming no agent lifecycle data was captured.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call depends on a schedulable pod and would not return vmIdPresent or remoteState if the pod is stuck pending.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod was never scheduled.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs=126899 is well under the outage threshold, so the failure is driven by the Unschedulable condition, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector rules (e.g., a required label such as a kata/peerpods node label is absent or was removed from those nodes), permanently reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource (2 of 6) may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling periods.

QUATERNARY — Pod resource request misconfiguration: the remote agent pod may be requesting more kata.peerpods.io/vm units than necessary, consuming slots faster than expected and accelerating exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient capacity exhaustion that self-resolved, not a persistent misconfiguration.

If sibling checks for non-remote agent features (e.g., local-agent-create) also failed at the same timestamp, a broader infrastructure or authentication issue would be more likely than a kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific capacity problem.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes and alerts when free slots fall below a minimum threshold (e.g., < 2 free slots), providing early warning before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote agent pod and warns if it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure earlier than the current 120s stuck-pod detection.

Consider adding a sibling-correlation eval rule: if all checks within the remote-agents feature fail with the same Unschedulable message pattern, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency (cluster capacity) alert rather than treating each check independently.

No evidence payloads (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were produced because agent creation never completed, so the state-polling step that depends on a live agent was never reached.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent VM never became schedulable and the runtime probe never reached the stage where it could return orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every eval pod submitted during this run window was stuck Unschedulable until the eval timeout was reached. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval checks in production-api and is not evidence of a user-facing outage on its own, as no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=153146, status=fail — the probe ran for ~153s before timing out, consistent with a pod that was never scheduled
failed-check.evidence: empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, confirming the agent VM never started

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent() could complete (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918)
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — this call submits the pod that the scheduler rejected
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes — concurrent eval runs, other workloads, or leaked/unreleased VM slots have consumed all available peer-pod VM capacity, leaving no room for new eval pods.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy; if those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, scheduling is impossible regardless of cluster size.

Tertiary: VM slot leak from a prior eval run — if a previous remote-agent eval pod was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may not have released the VM slot on an earlier failure), the slot could still be held, reducing available capacity.
Lower probability: Cluster autoscaler or node provisioner did not add a new kata-capable node in time — the eval timeout (~153s) may be shorter than the node scale-up latency for kata peer-pod nodes.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run only the remote-agent-runtime eval against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all cluster nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Identify which nodes advertise the resource, how many slots are allocatable, and how many are currently consumed.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm to find slot holders
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, ns: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
reproductionSteps.details: Determine whether prior eval pods or other workloads are holding VM slots that should have been released.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect node affinity/selector on a remote-agent pod spec to confirm which nodes are eligible
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the pod spec for a remote-agent eval pod (or the template used by createAgent) and compare its nodeSelector/affinity rules against the labels on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm only 2 are eligible.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together to confirm shared scheduling dependency
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm that all three checks fail with the same Unschedulable message, reinforcing the shared infrastructure dependency.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with identical Unschedulable scheduling errors (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, failed-check.message).
affectedAreas.details: Feature registered at infra/evals/status/features.json line 176; checks at lines 183-185.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes kata peer-pod VM scheduling layer (production-api cluster)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes and node affinity mismatch on 4/6 nodes is the direct blocking condition. This is a cluster infrastructure area, not application code.
affectedAreas.details: 0/6 nodes available; 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match pod affinity/selector; preemption found no victims.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner createAgent() call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId), which submits the pod that the scheduler rejected. No evidence was collected because this call never completed successfully.

affectedAreas.label: Remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence) because the agent pod never started and no response metadata was produced.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine whether exhaustion is ongoing or was transient.
Identify and terminate any leaked or zombie remote-agent eval pods that may be holding VM slots without active workloads.
Review the node affinity/selector configuration on remote-agent pods to determine whether additional nodes can be made eligible for scheduling, increasing available VM capacity.

Confirm that the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm slots even when the eval probe fails mid-execution (e.g., on timeout or API error).
Assess whether the kata peer-pod node pool needs additional nodes or higher VM slot limits to support concurrent eval runs without exhaustion.

Monitor the remote-agents feature health status: infra/evals/status/features.json shows degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2; with all 3 checks failing (2 required: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state), the feature may be in an outage state per the registry thresholds.

This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api environment. Confirm with on-call whether user-facing remote agent provisioning is also impacted before escalating as a user-facing incident.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether VM slot exhaustion is the active condition and how many slots remain available on each node.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Focus on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector.

recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, ns: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether leaked or long-running pods from prior eval runs are consuming the limited VM slots.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Look for pods in Running or Pending state that should have been cleaned up.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the failed expected-output contract after confirming node capacity
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is persistent or was transient; a pass after capacity is freed would confirm the exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels on all 6 cluster nodes to verify affinity eligibility
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms which nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity rules and whether the 4 non-matching nodes could be made eligible by label changes.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Cross-reference against the pod spec's affinity rules retrieved from the remote-agent pod template.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check for stuck or undeleted remote-agent eval pods from prior runs
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether the withCleanup path in run-status-probes.mjs failed to delete prior eval pods, leaving VM slots unreleased.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Relevant to the VM slot leak possible cause.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., API-level rejection, misconfigured resource request) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passed (or any remote-agents check passed) in a concurrent or immediately subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient race condition rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If the pod spec for remote-agent eval pods does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would point to a different root cause such as a node label mismatch or admission webhook rejection.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster intervention, it would suggest the failure was caused by a brief capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 is confirmed to have released all VM slots from prior runs, the VM slot leak hypothesis would be disproved as a contributing factor.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity before attempting remote-agent pod creation, and reports a distinct 'capacity-unavailable' status rather than timing out after 120-153s.
Add a VM slot leak detection eval that periodically scans for remote-agent eval pods older than a configurable TTL and alerts if any are found still holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, catching misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.

Consider a latency-banded eval that distinguishes between 'pod never scheduled' (scheduling failure) and 'pod scheduled but agent did not reach ready state' (VM boot or runtime failure), to improve diagnostic precision in future failures.
